claims.claim: An earthquake is caused by sudden slip on a fault after stress overcomes friction, releasing energy in waves that produce shaking.
Magnitude measures the size of an earthquake at its source and has one value on a given magnitude scale, while intensity measures shaking at a particular location and varies from place to place.
Seismometers record ground vibrations and their data are used to determine an earthquake’s time, location, and magnitude.
Shaking intensity is affected by factors including distance from rupture and local surface geology, so equal-magnitude earthquakes can produce different local experiences.
Earthquake science can describe hazards and quantify events, but a basic lesson cannot predict the precise time of a local earthquake.
